title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: Internal Transfers and the Excess Withdrawal Fee
content:
Internal transfers are how money moves between a customer's own accounts inside Piedmont Crescent Bank. This page explains how an internal transfer out of a Savings & Money Market Accounts product stands in relation to the excess withdrawal fee, and on what ground a fee charged on the transfer that opened a certificate of deposit is given back.

## Rule

**Channel.** A transfer from a savings or money market account that opens a certificate of deposit for the same owner posts as an internal transfer. The internal transfer channel is not one of the channels any tier counts toward its withdrawal allowance.

**Consequence for a fee.** An excess withdrawal fee charged on that transfer was therefore charged contrary to the savings charter. It is refunded in full on the bank-error ground.

**Standing of the refund.** Being a bank-error refund, it is subject to no time limit and does not count toward the customer's courtesy refund limit.

**Where the tier counts internal transfers.** If the account's tier did list internal transfers among its counted channels, nothing would be refunded under this policy.

## Condition table

| Tier counts internal transfers | Excess withdrawal fee on the funding transfer | Refund under this policy |
|---|---|---|
| no | charged | yes, in full, bank error |
| yes | charged | none |

## Points of judgement

**The fee posted eight months ago. Is it too late?** No. A bank-error refund has no deadline.

**The customer already used this year's courtesy refunds. Does that block this refund?** No. The courtesy limit does not apply to a bank-error refund, and this refund does not use it up.
